No `meta.json` change is owed (no new page). Right.
- **Governed surface:** `skills/**` is a Tier H register row; this record is the contract-tier review of record and the landing still needs an authorized approval and every check green. The PR is draft, authored by the fleet bot from the base repo (not a fork). Right.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/28256-data-skill-percent-display-lookup-autofill.md`: `'@objectstack/skills': patch`, body carries `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` as line-initial declarations; the PR body carries the same pair. Kind `none` ⇒ `patch` is the level the Post-Task Checklist prescribes; nothing else in the diff publishes. No `(narrowing)` arm, no `!` in the title, so no dogfood battery is owed. Matches what the diff publishes.

Clause-②: no

### ③ Boundary flags

The os-dev-report (comment 6550627372 on #28256) carries `open_questions: []` — nothing to answer. Its flags, each answered:

- **NOT MEASURED `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` (exit 3, needs a full build).** The diff touches no package entry, no `.ts`; CI's `Lint · repo & tooling gates` carries it and is still `in_progress` on this head. Accepted as a CI-owned reading; not a gap in the review.
- **`out_of_scope_findings[0]`: the `percent` row's When-to-Use text "Percentage values (0-100)" does not state the storage rule** (`percentScaleOf`: a fraction unless `max` is above 1; `scale`'s describe: a stored 0.25 reads `25%`). Confirmed on `main` and pre-dating both cards. It is a metadata-authoring trap in the Prime Directive #10 sense — an author reading "0-100" on a fraction-stored field writes 25 and sees 2500% — so it is escalated to the seat to **file as its own card** (dedupe words: percent row storage, percentScaleOf skill), not left as a PR note. Not this PR's defect; not a blocker here.
- **Not-touched list** (`evals/*`, `references/_index.md` under open PR #28467, `skills/objectstack-ui`): the objectstack-ui line "`autofill: false` opts one column out of the typeahead copy" (SKILL.md:102) stays consistent with the new text — both describe the grid's same-named copy. Confirmed correct as is. No eval case was asked by either card; the one eval token that touches a deleted example (`unique: 'organization'`, objects-fields-relationships.json:30) is still taught in `rules/indexing.md`.
- **The #28322 acceptance note asking this card to state the fully-authored master-detail bound** is honoured in `fields.mdx` (judged in ④).
- **CI families at report time: `in_progress`.** Still true at review time — see the check-run line in ④.

No flag escalates beyond the one card-to-file above.

### ④ Design judgment

**Check-runs on `0984e3e9` (the gate verdicts):** `success` — Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Build Core, Test UI, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, the three `Lint · scoped` jobs, Spec property liveness, Check Documentation Links, PR-body guards, Dogfood Regression Gate, Auto Label, Plan Test Core shards, filter. `in_progress` — Build Docs, Lint · CI/release & engine gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates (the job that carries `check-skills-token-ratchet`), Live E2E UI, Test Core 1/8–3/8, Type Check · consumer gates / debt ledger / source gates / workspace. `skipped` (path-filtered) — Build & E2E UI, Lint UI, Type Check UI, the UI shards, the opt-in harnesses. No check has failed. The ratchet and the docs guards are therefore not yet verdicts; my own reading of the tree is below.

#### `skills/objectstack-data/rules/field-types.md` — every teaching sentence against the spec and the code

- **`percent` row:** "`percentDisplay` — the read-only face: unset or `'bar'` draws a progress bar, `'plain'` the number alone, for a rate or a probability." Values: `z.enum(['bar','plain'])` — exact. Default: the describe says absent = the renderer default, a bar; `PercentCellRenderer` returns the bare `formatted` span only on the literal `'plain'`, every other value keeps the bar — exact. Read-only face: the describe scopes it to list cells and the record page and says display only; the renderer is the one every read-only host draws — exact. The row lists the key on `percent` only; the spec accepts it at parse on any type (no type restriction, by the TSDoc's own words), and the row makes no refusal claim, so nothing is over-taught. **Holds.**
- **`lookup` / `master_detail` rows list `lookupAutofill`:** the superRefine accepts the key on exactly those two types and refuses `multiple: true`; `user` and `tree` are not listed. **Holds.**
- **The paragraph under the Relational table**, clause by clause: shape `[{ target, source, overwrite? }]` and "single-value `lookup` / `master_detail`" — the strictObject and the superRefine, exact. "A pick copies the picked record's `source` into this object's `target`" and the example `[{ target: 'unit_price', source: 'list_price' }]` — the describe's own example. "In the form and the line-item grid" — `form.tsx` hands `onAutofill` and passes no `onSelectRecord`, so `LookupField` reads the pairs in a record form; `GridField` applies them in the line grid. "`target`: a field of this object an author writes (not the lookup, `readonly` or computed), named once" — the five refusals of `refuseDishonestLookupAutofill`, exact. "`source`: a declared, non-`internal` field of `reference` the target can hold" — `collectLookupAutofillErrors` plus `lookupAutofillTypeMismatch`, exact (the stack pass also waives the platform's injected audit columns, which the sentence does not mention — a narrower teaching, never a false one). "A pick fills an empty target or an earlier pick's fill; `overwrite: true` always replaces" — `declaredLookupAutofillPatch`'s three-way condition, exact. "Client-side only" — the describe's own clause; nothing on the write path reads it. "In a grid a declared target leaves the same-named `autofill` copy" — `lookupAutofillPatch` skips `declaredTargets` in the same-named loop, exact. **Holds in every clause.**
- **The blockquote** now names `vectorConfig` among keys "REFUSED at parse (`unrecognized_keys`)": `FieldSchema` is a `strictObject` and `vectorConfig` appears nowhere in `packages/spec/src`, so the refusal is exactly the unrecognised-key one. **Holds.**

#### The three deletions and the folded paragraph — does each rule keep a home?

- **`### Select with Default`** (`type: 'select'`, `required`, options with `default: true` and `color`): the Selection section of the same file keeps the options example with `default: true` and `color` (lines 82-87) and the table lists `options (value, label, color, default)`. No rule lost.
- **`### Email with Uniqueness`** (state the scope per ADR-0120; `'organization'` per-org and NULL-safe; `'global'` installation-wide; field-level bare `true` means `'organization'` and stays valid): `rules/indexing.md` § "Unique scope — always state it (ADR-0120)" carries all four — the two scopes and `COALESCE` NULL-safety at lines 53-54 and 70-74, the field-level `true` reading at 75-77 — and `SKILL.md:366` routes "unique scope" to that file. The `email` row still lists `unique` as a config. No rule lost.
- **`### Lookup (Many-to-Many)`** (`multiple: true`, `max: 10`): `SKILL.md:310` ("multi-value `lookup` (`multiple: true`) — an array column of ids") and the blockquote at 316-320 carry the multi-value lookup. The `max: 10` line taught nothing true: `FieldSchema.max` is "Maximum value… checked on the WRITTEN value" and no selection-cap key exists on a lookup, so the deletion removes a misleading example rather than a rule. No rule lost.
- **The vector paragraph** ("no `vectorConfig` block — refused at parse; `dimensions` is the flat key"): the refusal half now lives in the blockquote; the `vector` row ("`dimensions` (flat sibling, e.g. `1536`)") and the Vector example ("flat sibling") carry the other half. No rule lost.

**Re-wrap check:** the only pre-existing line whose break moved is the blockquote's, and it moved to insert `vectorConfig` (net +bytes), not to win room; the lookupAutofill paragraph is new text; every other hunk is a whole-block deletion or a one-cell table edit. No line was re-wrapped to buy room.

**Token reading (a reading of the tree, no gate run):** `wc -c` on `git show` of the file — `main` 12826 bytes = ceil(12826/4) = 3207; head 12824 bytes = 3206; the pinned ceiling at `check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs:690` is 3207. Within the ceiling by one token, as the PR states; the gate itself is still running in CI.

**Attempts to break it, none landing as must-fix:** (a) teaching `percentDisplay` on a type the renderer never draws — the row scopes it to `percent`; (b) a `user` field inheriting the key by "stored identically to `lookup`" — the row does not list it and the spec refuses it; (c) a `master_detail` with `multiple: true` — the paragraph says single-value; (d) the grid sentence read as "the column's `autofill` governs declared pairs" — the wording "leaves the same-named copy" says the opposite, matching the code.

#### `content/docs/data-modeling/fields.mdx` (docs face, the lookup section only — triage's one-PR exception, comment 6531273599)

- The code-block example, the property-table row ("single-value `lookup` / `master_detail` only") and the subsection's target rule (not the lookup, not `readonly`, not `formula`/`summary`/`autonumber`/`expression`, named once, "the object's parse refuses anything else") match `refuseDishonestLookupAutofill` exactly. The overwrite rule and the client-side-only paragraph are the describe's own. The grid paragraph matches `lookupAutofillPatch`. The link target `/docs/references/data/field` exists and carries both keys. **Holds.**
- "`os validate` / `os build` judge the source against the referenced object" — true, and the describe's own words; `defineStack` judges it too (`validateCrossReferences` runs inside `buildDefinedStack`), so the sentence under-states the refusal rather than mis-states it. Nit, no change required.
- **Should-fix 1 — the source type rule omits multiplicity.** The page says the rules are carried "in full" and lists "the same type, a string-valued field into a text target, `number` and `currency` into each other, a relationship only into a relationship over the same object". `lookupAutofillTypeMismatch`'s first refusal is "one holds a list and the other a single value" (a `multiple: true` or `multiselect`/`checkboxes`/`tags` source into a single-value target, or the reverse). The PR body says "same type and multiplicity"; the page says "the same type". Add "and multiplicity" (or "a list only into a list"). Nothing taught is false; one refusal is unlisted.
- **Should-fix 2 — the master-detail bound is worded looser than the code.** The page: "A master-detail collection whose relationship and every column are authored loads no child fields." `MasterDetailForm.tsx:1257-1259`: the fetch is skipped when `relationshipField` is set **and every column carries a `type`** (`columnsTyped`); an authored column without `type` triggers hydration, and such a grid does see the pairs (line 1358). Say "every column carries its `type`" — the #28322 acceptance note itself spells it "FK + every column typed". Harmless direction (an author expecting no fill gets one), so should-fix.
- Heading level `####` sits beside the existing `#### Referential integrity`; no tracker number appears in either hunk (`check:doc-authoring`); the identifiers named (`percentDisplay`, `lookupAutofill`, `target`, `source`, `overwrite`, `autofill`) all exist on `main`.

#### Out of scope, for the seat

- The `percent` row's "(0-100)" storage trap (③ above) — file a card; it is the file's pre-existing text, not this PR's.

No must-fix. Two should-fixes on the docs face (multiplicity in the type rule; "every column typed" in the bound), both one-phrase edits that leave the skill file and its token count untouched.

**VERDICT: PASS**
